newsitem.title: USA: U.S. asks Swiss consular help in Iran case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. asks Swiss consular help in Iran case.

text.p: The United States has asked Switzerland, its go-between with Iran, to check into reports that a U.S. citizen has been arrested in Iran, the State Department said on Wednesday.
If an American is being held, Swiss diplomats will ask for consular access on U.S. behalf, department spokesman John Dinger told a regular news briefing.

On Tuesday, the head of Iran's judiciary, Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi, said Iran had recently arrested a U.S. national for entering the country illegally, Iranian radio reported. No further details were made public.
Iran and the United States do not maintain diplomatic relations. Dinger said he did not have the name of the American reportedly arrested.
He said several U.S. citizens were being detained in Iran, most of them "dual nationals." Since none had provided a waiver of the U.S. Privacy Act, none could be identified publicly, Dinger added.

The United States advises its citizens against travel to Iran but if someone ignores this warning and gets into trouble there, "we will make every effort to assist that American through our protecting power of the Swiss," Dinger said.
He said the request to the Swiss had been made by the U.S. Embassy in Berne.
